H6IA04217.name: Dave Dawson
H6IA04217.bio: Prosecutor in the Woodbury County Attorney's Office and former member of the Iowa House of Representatives.

positions.stance: Will fight to lower prescription drug costs and expand rural health care access; supports allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices directly with pharmaceutical companies.
Will work to expand broadband, repair roads and bridges, strengthen family farms, make housing more affordable, and support small businesses.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage, passing the PRO Act, and "aggressive antitrust enforcement against the corporate monopolies" driving up prices.
Opposes any cut, privatization, or benefit reduction to Social Security or Medicare, and supports lifting the Social Security payroll tax cap.
Supports restoring the full strength of the Voting Rights Act and a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United.
Will work with the Trump administration to complete border enforcement, stop the flow of fentanyl, and support ICE enforcement and removal operations.
Supports protecting markets, defending landowner rights, and President Trump's efforts to secure free and fair trade agreements for farm goods.
Will join the administration in "standing up to China, bringing jobs back to America, and restoring energy independence."
Committed to advancing freedom at home and abroad, "including defending life from conception to natural death."
Committed to ensuring service members have the training, resources, and equipment they need, and to advocating for veterans.

H8NV03036.name: Dina Titus
H8NV03036.bio: U.S. Representative since 2008; former UNLV government professor for 34 years and Nevada state senator for 20 years.

H6NV01331.name: Carrie Buck
H6NV01331.bio: Nevada state senator; former teacher and school principal who led the growth of the Pinecrest Academy charter school network.

positions.stance: Will work in Congress to "protect parents' rights."
Will work in Congress to "secure the border."
Will work in Congress to "fully fund our police."
Will work in Congress to "ensure tips are never taxed."
Will "work with the President to hold Washington accountable for every taxpayer dollar."

H6NV02362.name: Teresa Benitez-Thompson
H6NV02362.bio: Former social worker, 12-year Nevada Assembly member and Majority Leader, and former chief of staff to Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford.

positions.stance: Says addressing family costs will be her "number one job"; plan includes restoring federal funds cut by DOGE, regulating AI-driven layoffs, and building workforce housing.
Supports protecting public lands; says land sales should occur "only through collaboration with local and tribal stakeholders" and wildfire funding cuts must be reversed.
Opposes the SAVE Act and supports expanding mail and early voting and investing in election infrastructure and cybersecurity.
"Healthcare should be as accessible and inexpensive as possible"; supports defending the Affordable Care Act and protecting reproductive freedom through federal legislation.
Says U.S. military aid to Israel "should not be unconditional" and supports phasing out direct financial support for offensive arms sales.

H4NV04108.name: David Flippo
H4NV04108.bio: Retired U.S. Air Force officer and Nevada small business owner.

positions.stance: Will "cut wasteful Washington spending to fight inflation," slash regulations, expand American energy production, and deliver tax cuts.
Supports banning "males from girls' and women's sports" and protecting single-sex spaces in schools and public facilities.
Will "fully fund and back the Blue," enact tough sentencing for violent and repeat offenders, and end soft-on-crime policies.
Supports deporting illegal immigrants, passing the SAVE Act, and ending catch-and-release and sanctuary policies.
Will "defend water rights, grazing, mining, and public lands" and improve rural roads, broadband, and energy access.

H6NV04020.name: Susie Lee
H6NV04020.bio: U.S. Representative since 2018; former president of Communities In Schools of Nevada and founding director of After-School All-Stars in Las Vegas.

positions.stance: Supports "legislation to codify the right to choose."

H4NV03225.name: Martin O'Donnell
H4NV03225.bio: Composer and audio producer; founder of O'Donnell/Salvatori Inc. and former audio director and composer at Bungie.

positions.stance: Will fight for an economy that "prioritizes American workers," with added safeguards and protections for workers as automation and AI expand.
Supports "ending the magnets that cause illegal immigration," building what is needed for border control, and targeting human and drug trafficking.
Wants a return to when "one good job was enough to raise a family" and will work to ensure "government stays out of your way."
Supports acting now "to bend the cost curve on government programs and working toward a balanced budget."

H2NV04011.name: Steven Horsford
H2NV04011.bio: U.S. Representative serving on the House Ways and Means Committee; former head of the Culinary Training Academy.

positions.stance: Supports the TIP Improvement Act "to make sure tipped workers keep more of the money they earn."
Fighting to pass the HOME Act "to make owning a home possible again" and ensure access to safe and affordable housing.
Fighting to pass the RELIEF Act so Nevada families and businesses affected by tariffs he calls illegal "get their money back."
"No Nevadan should go bankrupt because they get sick"; fighting to protect and expand access to affordable health care.
Fighting to "expand apprenticeships, fully fund schools, and invest in Nevada's future."

H6NV04111.name: Cody Whipple
H6NV04111.bio: Fourth-generation Nevadan, small business owner, and rancher.

positions.stance: Make "housing, healthcare, groceries, and energy more affordable."
Protect tipped workers "by eliminating taxes on tips and defending overtime pay."
Vote for the best policies for Nevada and "stand up to the political party boss power grabs."
"Eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse to protect this vital safety net."
"Expand quality education and career pathways for every Nevada student."

H0AR01083.name: Rick Crawford
H0AR01083.bio: U.S. Representative for Arkansas' 1st District and U.S. Army veteran who served as an Explosive Ordnance Disposal technician.

positions.stance: Says his "top priority" is to address the debt crisis "by enacting permanent spending controls."
Asks supporters to join him "as we lower taxes, grow our economy, and fight for the conservative values Arkansans hold."
Will "fight to keep an over zealous federal government off our backs and out of our backyard's."

H6AR01155.name: Terri Yarbrough
H6AR01155.bio: Board-certified pathologist and laboratory medical director.

positions.stance: Believes "no one is above the law" and that "Checks and balances are not obstacles. They are guardrails."
"We have to get dark money out of politics. Period."
Supports "free, fair, transparent elections where every vote counts and every voter has confidence in the outcome."
Supports family farms and "pushing back on big monopolies," and "Raising the minimum wage so work actually pays."
Supports "Accessible, affordable healthcare so getting sick does not mean going broke," including maternity care closer to home.

H4AR02141.name: French Hill
H4AR02141.bio: Chairman of the U.S. House Financial Services Committee; former community banker and founder and CEO of Delta Trust & Banking Corp.

positions.stance: Cites helping pass the Working Families Tax Cut, including eliminating taxes on tips and overtime, and introducing the Price Stability Act to lower costs.
Backed the Secure the Border Act and No Sanctuary for Criminals Act and supported the Laken Riley Act; says "All states are border states."
Co-sponsored the Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2025 and the Major Richard Star Act to expand benefits for combat-injured veterans.
Sponsored the Social Security Fairness Act and helped pass a new tax deduction for seniors, including on Social Security income.
Introduced the Flatside Wilderness Act to set aside wilderness in Perry County, later expanded by 2,200 national forest acres.

H6AR02286.name: Chris Jones
H6AR02286.bio: Science and technology professional who grew up in Pine Bluff, Arkansas.

positions.stance: Will increase "the availability of safe, affordable housing options for homeowners, renters, and first-time buyers" and bring home energy costs down.
Will expand access to quality, affordable health care and lower out-of-pocket costs for individuals and working families.
Will "Invest in education, workforce training, and lifelong learning opportunities."
Will "Strengthen retirement security, through savings opportunities and secure retirement planning."
Will promote "affordable, accessible childcare options that support working families."

H0AR03055.name: Steve Womack
H0AR03055.bio: U.S. Representative since 2010 and Appropriations subcommittee chairman; former Mayor of Rogers and retired Arkansas Army National Guard colonel.

positions.stance: Will "end gerrymandering, protect voting rights, and ensure every eligible Arkansan can vote freely and fairly."
Says leadership means "telling the truth and putting people first, not profiting from office, protecting party power, or manipulating voters."
"Elections should be decided by voters, not by corporations and billionaires who can pour in unlimited money."
"Faith doesn't mean we all believe the same thing. It means we believe in each other, even when politics tries to divide us."
Supports easing everyday expenses and lowering housing costs to "make sure families can get ahead."

H4AR04048.name: Bruce Westerman
H4AR04048.bio: U.S. Representative for Arkansas' 4th District who describes himself as the only forester in the House.

positions.stance: Says he helped "roll back more than a dozen job-killing Obama-era regulations" and stood up to an overreaching federal bureaucracy.
"We must keep taxes lower, so that individuals can invest into their small businesses and families can make ends meet."
Supports science-based management of national forests; introduced the Resilient Federal Forests Act.
Introduced the Fair Care Act, whose goal is to "cover more Americans and lower the costs they pay for healthcare."

H6AR04084.name: James Russell
H6AR04084.bio: Co-owner of an outpatient mental health business in Little Rock; former Arkansas State Medical Board credentialing specialist and Arkansas National Guard member.

positions.stance: Says leaders "should go to town halls, not just big money events" and should follow the Constitution.
Supports "fair laws that raise wages, make sure everyone gets equal pay for equal work, and treat all workers fairly."
"Working people should pay less, and the rich should pay their fair share"; supports closing tax loopholes.
Supports "expanding Medicare and moving toward healthcare for everyone."
Supports making sure "everyone can get a good, free education," including college or job training.

H6MS01131.name: Trent Kelly
H6MS01131.bio: U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 1st District since winning a 2015 special election.

H6MS01313.name: Cliff Johnson
H6MS01313.bio: Attorney at the MacArthur Justice Center at the University of Mississippi School of Law; former U.S. Department of Justice attorney in Mississippi.

positions.stance: "Combat inflation and the policies that are driving up costs for all Mississippians."
Ensure North Mississippi "gets its fair share of federal dollars for economic development, infrastructure, and struggling Mississippi schools."
Fight "a rigged political system where only corporations and wealthy donors have a voice."
"Preserve the core rights promised to all Americans– especially the right to have your vote count."

H4MS02068.name: Bennie Thompson
H4MS02068.bio: U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 2nd District since 1993 and Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee; former Mayor of Bolton.

positions.stance: "A steadfast supporter of farmers, Bennie has never voted against a Farm Bill in his time in Congress."
Says all 23 counties in the district are medically underserved; "Bennie fights for coverage families can afford."
Believes courts "should provide rulings of non-biased justice" and citizens should live without "encroachment on their civil rights."
"Standing with the millions of Americans who served, and the families who served beside them."
"Supports reauthorizing the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, including Title I, Part A."

H2MS02203.name: Ron Eller
H2MS02203.bio: Twenty-year military veteran who has worked in the private health care sector and started manufacturing businesses.

positions.stance: Says the nation must "raise and train the next generation of leaders, inventors, scientists, and entrepreneurs"; supports prison reform to make inmates productive.
Calls for "fair taxation with good representation" and says "An America first policy is critical."
"We need all forms of energy"; says the U.S. "can not and should not cut our use of fossil fuels."
Says the Second Amendment "must be defended" and concealed carry licenses should be valid across all jurisdictions.
Opposes government funding for abortion providers and supports Mississippi's law allowing abortion only to save the life of the mother.

H8MS03125.name: Michael Guest
H8MS03125.bio: U.S. Representative since 2018 and chairman of the House Ethics Committee; former District Attorney for Madison and Rankin Counties.

positions.stance: Committed to "free market economic policies of lower taxes, fewer regulations."
Supports "the right to life of the unborn."
Committed to promoting constitutional freedoms, including "our 2nd Amendment rights."
Says he has worked "to strengthen our agricultural community."
Says he has "fought for stronger border security to stop illegal immigration and drugs."

H6MS03228.name: Michael Chiaradio
H6MS03228.bio: Farmer and entrepreneur who raises livestock in Shubuta, Mississippi; former team supervisor at a global public company.

positions.stance: Says "Simply raising taxes or cutting spending does not solve our problems"; supports investing in factories, farms, infrastructure, and a broader safety net.
"Every American should have access to high quality preventive and curative healthcare at a low cost"; supports training more health care workers.
Supports expanding USDA homebuilding programs, investing in modern infrastructure, and strengthening small agricultural producers.
Supports favorable loans, qualified debt forgiveness, and expanded rental programs to help small farms access machinery and diversify crops.
Supports federal investment to replace aging grid infrastructure with modern transmission lines, storm-hardened equipment, and advanced cybersecurity.

H2MS04258.name: Mike Ezell
H2MS04258.bio: Former Jackson County Sheriff with more than 40 years in law enforcement.

positions.stance: Believes in "the right to life of the unborn" and will fight to "put a stop to taxpayer-funded abortions."
Will "fight any and all efforts to defund the police" and make sure law enforcement has the support it needs.
Will "work to finish Trump's wall" and oppose catch-and-release policies.
Will fight to "take power away from Washington," protect religious freedom, and oppose legislation taking away the right to bear arms.
Will oppose cuts to the defense budget and "work to clean up bureaucracy" so veterans are treated with respect and dignity.

H6MS04242.name: Jeffrey Hulum III
H6MS04242.bio: Former U.S. Army Sergeant Major and 22-year Army veteran from Gulfport, Mississippi.

positions.stance: Wants "an economy that works for working people, not just for corporations and the wealthy" where families can earn a living wage.
"Every child deserves a quality education, no matter their ZIP code."
"No family should go broke to see a doctor or afford life-saving medication."
Supports a justice system that keeps communities safe "while ensuring fairness, accountability, and rehabilitation."
Says "civil rights, voting rights, and basic freedoms" must be protected for all Mississippians.

H0KS01123.name: Tracey Mann
H0KS01123.bio: Former Lieutenant Governor of Kansas; fifth-generation Kansan raised on a family farm.

positions.stance: "I believe that life begins at conception"; will oppose taxpayer funding of abortions.
Will "stand up against efforts to diminish or weaken the rights of law-abiding Americans to own, carry and use firearms."
Supports free and fair trade, crop insurance, and adding value to Kansas farm products; intends "to serve as a champion for free trade."
"I support the President in his efforts to Make America Great Again."
Says rural communities must "not just survive but thrive" and "access to broadband throughout the district is critical."

H6KS01203.name: Lauren Reinhold
H6KS01203.bio: Attorney and former Attorney Advisor at the Social Security Administration.

positions.stance: "Rural hospitals are the life blood of our communities"; prioritizes rebuilding rural health care.
Farm families "deserve a system that prioritizes producers, family operations" and small businesses "over corporate monopolies."
Says the economy prospers when it "stops favoring corporate monopolies and starts honoring the dignity of a hard day's work."
"Kansans deserve a government of the people, by the people, and for the people."
Supports reform "that secures our borders while providing a fair path to citizenship for those already contributing to our communities."
